questions.q: In the SigninLogs table, what does ResultType represent?
options: Whether a sign-in succeeded ("0") or failed (a non-zero code)
The region the sign-in request originated from
The name of the analytics rule that will process the event
The severity level Sentinel will assign to any resulting alert
questions.explain: ResultType equal to "0" marks a successful sign-in; any non-zero value marks a failure of some kind.

questions.q: What is the real limitation of the first query — filtering to failures, grouping by user and a 10-minute bin, then keeping counts over 5?
options: It only counts failures and doesn't check whether a success actually followed them
It cannot run on a schedule at all
It returns every sign-in regardless of ResultType
It requires entity mapping before it can execute
questions.explain: This count-only query fires on any user with 5+ failures in 10 minutes, whether or not a success ever followed.

questions.q: What does the join kind=inner step between Failures and Successes accomplish in the finished query?
options: It lines up each flagged user's failure cluster with their own successful sign-ins so a following success can be checked
It permanently deletes all failure records from the table
It changes the rule's run frequency
It converts the query into a built-in analytics rule template
questions.explain: The join matches each user's failure cluster against their own successes so the next filter can check timing.

questions.q: What does the filter "SuccessTime > LastFailure and SuccessTime < LastFailure + 10m" enforce?
options: That a success landed after the failure cluster and within a bounded window of it — the sequence-aware requirement
That the user has never had a single failed sign-in
That the rule only runs once every 10 minutes
That IPAddress must match between the failure and the success
questions.explain: This is the KQL enforcement of the "after the failures" requirement from the correlation-rule pseudocode.

questions.q: Once this finished query is pasted into a Scheduled Analytics Rule, what else from this chapter completes the rule?
options: The run schedule and alert threshold from Lesson 9, plus entity mapping from Lesson 11
Nothing else is needed — the query alone is a complete rule with no other settings
A separate custom connector that only applies to built-in templates
Deleting the SigninLogs table from the workspace
questions.explain: The schedule and threshold control when it runs and alerts, and entity mapping makes the resulting alert's account and IP trackable entities.
